claims.text: Nvidia's Groq 3 LPX inference rack has entered full production, with Nebius as its first cloud launch partner.
claims.reasoning: Nvidia's own newsroom release (Tier 0) states full production verbatim and names Nebius as launch partner; the release itself quotes Nebius's own CTO directly, so this is not one-sided vendor messaging -- Nebius cooperated in the announcement. CNBC's same-day, on-record coverage independently corroborates.

claims.text: Nvidia says broader deployment of Groq 3 LPX racks, including through Nebius, will begin before the end of 2026.
claims.reasoning: This specific timeline ("online this year") traces to an on-record quote from Nvidia senior director Dion Harris to CNBC. Nvidia's own release is more conservative -- it says Nebius "plans to" bring the rack onto its Token Factory platform without committing to a firm date. Confirmed as a statement Nvidia made (one on-record Tier-2 quote suffices for an announcement/statement claim); the article attributes the 'this year' timeline to Nvidia's statement rather than presenting it as a locked commitment.

claims.text: Nvidia's relationship with Groq stems from a deal reported in December 2025 at roughly $20 billion; Nvidia said at the time it was licensing Groq's inference IP and hiring key Groq staff -- including founder Jonathan Ross and president Sunny Madra -- rather than acquiring Groq as a company, and Groq has continued to operate independently.
claims.reasoning: Two independent Tier-2 sources: CNBC's Dec 24, 2025 report broke the ~$20B figure and initially framed it as an acquisition; TrendForce's Dec 29, 2025 report carries Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's on-record correction ('we are not acquiring Groq as a company... licensing Groq's IP' and hiring staff). The falsifier pass caught that the original verifier draft would have flatly called this an 'acquisition,' which Nvidia itself disputed -- corrected before publication. Included as dated background, not presented as new news.

claims.text: Nvidia says the Groq 3 LPX rack delivers about 3,400 output tokens per second at 100K context on Gemma 4 31B, roughly four times faster than the nearest alternative, per an Artificial Analysis benchmark Nvidia cited in its announcement.
claims.reasoning: Figure is sourced to a benchmark Nvidia itself cites, not independently reproduced by press. The Register's same-day piece scrutinizes but does not dispute the number; it notes the test used a comparatively small, dense model (arguably a best case) and that Nvidia needs 64+ chips to match throughput a rival (Cerebras) hits with 1-2 chips on other workloads, with larger-model performance untested. Labeled vendor-claim per policy; Register's caveats included in the body for balance.

falsifier_notes: Falsifier direct-fetched the Nvidia release and confirmed 'full production' and the Nebius quote are verbatim, not paraphrase -- claim 1 survives.
